# issue 4710 -- which guard emits the diagnostic, and what has run by then
# generator: probe-pass-order.py (committed beside this file)
# diagnostic: Index for resource array inside cbuffer must be a literal expression

== step 1: dxc's own pass ordering ==
$ dxc -T ps_6_0 -E psMain -Odump repro.hlsl
  exit=0x00000000
    [ 33] -hlsl-dxil-promote-local-resources
    [ 34] -hlsl-dxil-promote-static-resources
    [ 35] -invalidate-undef-resource
    [ 36] -dxilgen  <<<
    [ 37] -hlsl-dxil-precise
    [ 38] -simplify-inst
    [ 39] -scalarizer
    [ 40] -dxil-elim-vector
    [ 41] -dxil-loop-unroll,MaxIterationAttempt=1024,OnlyWarnOnFail=0,StructurizeLoopExits=1  <<<
    [ 42] -loop-unroll,StructurizeLoopExits=1
    [ 43] -simplify-inst
  -dxilgen is at 36; -dxil-loop-unroll is at 41
  -> the pass holding the guard runs BEFORE the pass that implements [unroll]
  Same fact in source: lib/Transforms/IPO/PassManagerBuilder.cpp,
  addHLSLPasses() adds createDxilGenerationPass(...) and only afterwards
  createDxilLoopUnrollPass(...), under the comment '// Passes to handle [unroll]'.

== step 2: does the front end reject it? ==
$ dxc -T ps_6_0 -E psMain -fcgl repro.hlsl -Fc scratch-fcgl.ll
  exit=0x00000000   diagnostic present: False
  -> No. -fcgl stops before the DXIL passes and the shader is accepted,
     so this is not a Sema/language rule despite the file:line:col shape.

== step 3: replay the SHIPPED pass list and capture the call stack ==
$ cdb -c "sxe -c \"kn 18; gh\" e0000001; g; q" dxopt -o=scratch-order-shipped.bc scratch-fcgl.ll <37 passes>
  exit=0x00000001
  guard 'GetBindingForResourceInCB' on the stack: True
  frames (trimmed to the relevant chain):
    dxcompiler!llvm_assert+0x51
    dxcompiler!hlsl::dxilutil::EmitWarningOrErrorOnInstruction+0x165
    dxcompiler!hlsl::dxilutil::EmitErrorOnInstruction+0x36
    dxcompiler!hlsl::HLModule::GetBindingForResourceInCB+0xbe
    dxcompiler!HLObjectOperationLowerHelper::CreateResourceForCbPtr+0x429
    dxcompiler!HLObjectOperationLowerHelper::GetOrCreateResourceForCbPtr+0xae
    dxcompiler!`anonymous namespace'::TranslateResourceInCB+0xe0
    dxcompiler!`anonymous namespace'::TranslateCBAddressUserLegacy+0x11c5
    dxcompiler!`anonymous namespace'::TranslateCBGepLegacy+0x1304
    dxcompiler!`anonymous namespace'::TranslateCBAddressUserLegacy+0x14bc
    dxcompiler!`anonymous namespace'::TranslateCBOperationsLegacy+0x114
    dxcompiler!TranslateHLSubscript+0xef
    dxcompiler!TranslateSubscriptOperation+0xf5
    dxcompiler!TranslateHLBuiltinOperation+0x845
    dxcompiler!hlsl::TranslateBuiltinOperations+0x290
    dxcompiler!`anonymous namespace'::DxilGenerationPass::GenerateDxilOperations+0x1b7
    dxcompiler!`anonymous namespace'::DxilGenerationPass::runOnModule+0x509
  NOTE: dxopt has no thread file system, so llvm::errs() asserts while
  printing the message -- the assert is the diagnostic being emitted, not a
  separate failure. dxc.exe prints the same message and exits 0x80004005.

== step 4: hoist [unroll] above -dxilgen -- NEGATIVE RESULT, read the self-check ==
$ dxopt -o=scratch-order-hoisted.bc scratch-fcgl.ll <116 passes, -dxil-loop-unroll moved to index 36>
  exit=0x00000000   diagnostic present: False
  produced a module: True
  SELF-CHECK: textureLoad calls = 1, SRV createHandle calls = 1
              the source loop has 4 iterations, so a faithful unroll owes 4 of each
    ; FooBars.0.Texture.0               texture     f32          2d      T0             t0     1
  -> The hoist did NOT faithfully unroll the loop: iterations are missing.
     It therefore says NOTHING about whether reordering would be a fix,
     and is recorded here only so the absence of the diagnostic in this
     arm is not mistaken for one.

== what this file establishes ==
  1. The diagnostic comes from DxilGenerationPass (a DXIL-lowering pass),
     not from Sema, and the guard is !CbPtr->hasAllConstantIndices().
  2. By the time that guard runs, [unroll] has not been applied, so the loop
     induction variable is still a non-constant SSA value.
  It does NOT establish what the right fix is, or whether the restriction is
  intended. That is a design decision, not a measurement.
